answer: Forced-Divergence Session Challenge. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge from its own private state, and peers compare a ripple of prior answers: a clone must replay identical history, so the first divergent probe exposes it. Honest agents keep a karst of unique private randomness; copies share none. Attacker cost: one live, separately maintained state stream plus unique entropy per identity, making N clones cost N real workloads. Sybils can share a haven only until probed, then split.
